reason: The iron-group core no longer has fusion support, so gravity should drive its collapse.
expectation: The core will collapse into dense matter.

effect: The iron core is collapsing into neutron-rich matter; dense-matter pressure may now affect its collapse.
reaction: The conversion of electrons and protons into neutrons is striking.
reason: Pressure in dense neutron-rich matter plausibly acts on the collapsing core.
expectation: The dense core will resist further collapse, producing a rebound or a neutron-star remnant.

effect: The neutron star is established, leaving the scattering of the outer layers as the remaining goal.
reaction: It is useful to see that not every massive stellar remnant has the same fate.
reason: The neutrino flood may help drive an explosion through the star's layered interior, though the exact pairing is a guess.
expectation: The neutrinos will help scatter the enriched stellar layers.

effect: The layered interior has no available combination, so my proposed explosion pairing was wrong.
reaction: The failure leaves the neutrinos' role unclear.
reason: Inspecting the neutrino flood should reveal its available partner and help identify how to scatter the layers.
expectation: The inspection will identify an available partner for the neutrinos, possibly triggering a combination.

effect: The neutrinos combined with the collapsing core to produce an outward supernova shock, suggesting the shock can now reach the star's layers.
reaction: The inspection clarified the neutrinos' role after my failed guess.
reason: The outward shock should travel through and scatter the enriched burning shells.
expectation: The shock will eject the star's enriched layers.

effect: The shock scattered the enriched layers as expanding ejecta, completing the remaining goal while leaving the neutron star behind.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the shock connect the explosion to the enriched debris.

mostWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the neutrino flood clarified how energy deposition can help revive an outward shock, and led directly to scattering the layers.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempt to combine the burning shells with neutrinos gave little explanation of why the pairing was unavailable.

surprise.text: The collapsing core could still combine with neutrinos after producing a neutron star, making an outward shock.

arbitrary.text: The failed shell–neutrino pairing felt somewhat opaque until inspection revealed that the collapsing core was the required partner.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow the enriched ejecta into the formation of later material; the shock explanation made that progression interesting.
